source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 44 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, which places it fifteenth in Virginia by published megawatts.

The campus carries 420,000 square feet of technical space and seven certifications, including SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and TIA-942. Each certification is a permission to host a category of work, not evidence that any particular tenant is present. The operator publishes no address, no tenant list, no power procurement method, and no delivery schedule.

Virginia is the largest published market in this dataset, with 2,563.4 MW across 29 facilities that publish a figure, out of 376 mapped facilities in the state. The gap between 376 mapped facilities and 29 with published megawatts is the more important number. Most of the physical buildout in the densest data center state in the country is invisible in capacity terms, and the facilities that do publish are the ones large enough to be counted.

The 44 MW figure does not translate directly into accelerator count. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it implies roughly 1,100 racks, but that is an assumption about density rather than a claim by CyrusOne. The same capacity at a traditional 8 kW per rack would be about 5,500 racks. The campus is sized to matter at either density, and the number that would settle the question is one the operator has not published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
